next_question: Should the Physics lane pivot to production SPAs with hash-based client-side routing (e.g., TodoMVC hash-SPA variants, React Router history-based SPAs) where multiple client-side states can share the same URL path, reducing URL-level leakage below 40% and enabling >=50 non-leakage transitions for PMI analysis?
why_next: This experiment confirms the parent's recommendation to pivot away from server-rendered MPAs: structural URL-level leakage (78-92%) on Wikipedia/MDN/GitHub makes the NL filter unworkable. Even with unlimited collection, 50 NL transitions at 92% leakage requires ~625 raw transitions. The PMI pipeline itself is validated (positive control BC 1.841 p=0.001) but cannot be applied to the tiny NL subsets (8/4/2 transitions) on these sites. Production SPAs with hash-based routing where multiple client-side states share the same URL path would naturally reduce leakage below 40%, enabling >=50 NL transitions at manageable raw collection sizes (~83 raw at 40% leakage). The synthetic-to-real gap remains the dominant unknown; the next experiment must address it by testing on genuine SPAs rather than continuing locally-hosted synthetic FSM experiments or server-rendered MPAs.

established: Server-rendered MPAs (Wikipedia/MDN/GitHub) have structural URL-level leakage of 78-92% where action.target_href == state_after.url by construction for link-based navigation. This is a fundamental property of <a href> on these sites, not a measurement artifact (audit V2, result.json observations).

After NL filtering on server-rendered MPAs, the remaining subsets are too small for PMI analysis: Wikipedia 8 NL (6 unique SA pairs, all singleton under Laplace alpha=1.0), GitHub 4 NL, MDN 2 NL. BC PMI = 0.0 bits is mathematically forced by SA-sparsity (audit V3).

The PMI pipeline (BC estimator, within-strata permutation, cross-trajectory shuffle) correctly detects known deterministic structure: synthetic 8-state SPA positive control BC PMI = 1.841 bits, permutation p = 0.001, determinism accuracy = 1.0 (result.json controls, audit V7).

The 3-condition ordered sequence from parent experiments (unique-content 0.493 > many-to-one 0.226 > fully-ambiguous 0.0 bits) provides clean quantitative decomposition of aliasing vs genuine PMI on the locally-hosted 3-state stochastic branching FSM.

Wikipedia H(S_next | URL) = 0.647 bits on all 91 transitions (exceeding 0.2 threshold) but H = 0.0 on the 8 NL transitions only, confirming the ceiling exists on full data but vanishes in the NL subset (result.json controls.C8_CEILING).

Frozen decision_rule C7 (>=50 NL per site on >=2/3 sites) correctly triggers MEASUREMENT_INVALID: 0/3 sites pass. This is an infrastructure/data-sufficiency failure, not scientific falsification (audit V1).
rejected: Server-rendered MPAs as testbed for C-WEB-DYNAMICS title-aware PMI: rejected due to structural URL-level leakage (78-92%) making NL subsets too small for analysis. Site selection must target SPAs with client-side routing.

Global title-shuffle as valid negative control implementation: audit V5 finds it is misimplemented (should be within-strata, not global) and PASS is trivial when perm_std=0 (frozen pass criterion |BC|<3*std AND std>0 unsatisfiable when std=0).
Partial state discrimination as PMI source: the parent's 3-condition sequence (0.493 → 0.226 → 0.0) on the stochastic branching FSM established this is eliminated when content is constant.
unknown: Whether production SPAs with hash-based client-side routing exhibit URL-level leakage <40% enabling >=50 NL transitions for PMI analysis (requires SPA corpus survey before experiment design).
Whether form submissions, button clicks, and JavaScript-triggered navigation on SPAs produce non-link-leakage transitions at rates sufficient for PMI analysis.
Whether title-aware PMI adds marginal information beyond URL-only on genuine SPAs where titles vary independently of URL path (requires per-URL title variance >1, not just global title diversity).

Whether the PMI pipeline can detect predictive structure on genuinely stochastic production SPA transitions (all prior tests are synthetic or locally-hosted; the synthetic-to-real gap remains the dominant unknown across 30+ experiments).
Whether the Bonferroni threshold inconsistency (spec says 0.0125 = alpha/4, code uses 0.00833 = alpha/6) affects any future decision and should be re-frozen consistently.
do_not_assume: Do not assume C-WEB-DYNAMICS is falsified — it concerns real Web dynamics and remains untested on production SPAs. MEASUREMENT_INVALID means the measurement infrastructure failed, not that the hypothesis is wrong.

Do not assume that BC PMI = 0.0 on Wikipedia NL transitions means titles carry no predictive information — the result is mathematically forced by SA-sparsity (8 transitions, 6 singleton SA pairs under Laplace alpha=1.0), not by genuine absence of title information.

Do not assume the PMI pipeline is production-ready — it is validated only on deterministic in-memory synthetic data (8-state SPA). No experiment has demonstrated PMI detection on genuinely stochastic real-web transitions.

Do not generalize the structural leakage finding beyond server-rendered MPAs with <a href> navigation — SPAs with hash routing, form submissions, and button clicks may exhibit fundamentally different leakage profiles.

Do not assume the frozen MEASUREMENT_INVALID verdict reflects scientific falsification of Web dynamics — the frozen decision rule's precedence (C7 checked first) masks the fact that the underlying effect is untested, not absent.

Do not continue locally-hosted synthetic FSM experiments for hash-based content observation — the parent's 3-condition sequence (0.493 → 0.226 → 0.0) closes that pathway. The next experiment must address the synthetic-to-real gap.

Do not assume URL-only PMI = 0.0 on Wikipedia NL reflects genuine absence of dynamical structure — Wikipedia H(S_next | URL) = 0.647 on all 91 transitions, indicating structure exists before leakage filtering.

recommended_action: Target production SPAs with hash-based client-side routing (TodoMVC hash-SPAs, React Router SPAs, Vue Router SPAs) where multiple client-side states share the same URL path, reducing URL-level leakage below 40%. Before designing the next experiment: (1) survey 3-5 candidate SPAs to measure empirical leakage rates; (2) fix Playwright EPIPE for higher throughput (50+ trajectories per site); (3) fix permutation protocol (within-strata, 1000 per stratum); (4) fix negative control (within-strata shuffle, strict pass criterion); (5) reconcile Bonferroni threshold (alpha/4 vs alpha/6). The next experiment should test title-aware PMI on genuine SPAs where the NL threshold is achievable, directly addressing the dominant synthetic-to-real gap. If no production SPA is accessible, a per-session hash pool design on the synthetic FSM could theoretically detect session-correlated genuine dynamics before production investment, but the parent handoff recommends against further locally-hosted synthetic FSM experiments.
